mainTopic: Hidden forms of רבית: mortgaged fields, רבא's three rejected practices, and half-profit partnerships in the new משנה
overview: This amud finishes the argument over whether a lender may hold a mortgaged field (a משכנתא) and eat its produce for a fixed yearly deduction from the debt. The side that permits it compares it to redeeming a שדה אחוזה from הקדש at a fixed price. The side that forbids it answers that a loan between people looks like רבית. רב אשי then brings two teachings from the elders of מתא מחסיא: an unspecified משכנתא lasts at least a year, and the field 'resides' with the lender, which matters for the law of בר מצרא. Next, רבא rejects three practices: רב פפא's higher price for delayed payment, the documents of מחוזא that wrote expected profit into the loan, and the leases of נרש where the borrower rented back his own mortgaged field. Along the way, רב אשי shows why even אמימר's careful use of such documents fails once the lender dies, and a newer lease wording is rejected. A new משנה then forbids half-profit deals with a storekeeper or an animal raiser unless the worker is paid, but allows taking calves and foals to raise for half without an appraisal. The גמרא begins by explaining that the wage is that of a פועל בטל and asks what that means.

steps.title: The permitting side finishes its proof from a redeemed ancestral field
steps.stepSummary: The one who permits a משכנתא with a fixed deduction finishes his comparison: a שדה אחוזה is redeemed for a fixed yearly sum, and here too a fixed deduction is fine.
steps.simpleTranslation: He redeems it for four זוזים a year. Here too, it is no different.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing the argument of the one who permits the fixed deduction. He says this case is just like redeeming a field from הקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When someone redeems a שדה אחוזה from הקדש, he pays a fixed price for each year, even if the field's produce is worth more. In the same way, the lender may take the produce for a fixed deduction from the loan, even if he ends up getting more than he deducted. A set price agreed ahead of time is not counted as profit on a loan.

keyTerms.meaning: an inherited family field that was given to הקדש

phrases.english: he redeems it for four zuz [a year],
here too, it is no different.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the permitting opinion's comparison to שדה אחוזה, which began just before this point.
steps.raayaObject: That a משכנתא with a fixed yearly deduction is permitted
steps.raayaSupportSource: Redeeming a שדה אחוזה from הקדש at a fixed yearly price, no matter what the produce is worth

steps.title: The forbidding side says הקדש is different from a loan
steps.stepSummary: The one who forbids answers that a שדה אחוזה belongs to הקדש and the Torah set up its redemption price. A loan between people is different, so here it looks like רבית.
steps.simpleTranslation: The one who forbids will tell you: a שדה אחוזה is הקדש, and the Torah set it up as a redemption. Here it is a loan, and it looks like רבית.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows how the forbidding side rejects the proof. He says the two cases are not alike.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With הקדש there is no loan at all. The Torah itself made a fixed redemption price, so there is no question of profit on a loan. In a משכנתא there really is a loan, so the lender taking produce worth more than the deduction looks like being paid for waiting for his money, which is רבית.

keyTerms.meaning: property belonging to the בית המקדש
the Merciful One, meaning the Torah

steps.whatToRemember: Permitting side: a fixed deduction is like the fixed redemption price of a שדה אחוזה. Forbidding side: הקדש has a price set by the Torah, but a loan between people with extra produce looks like רבית.

phrases.english: And the one who forbids will tell you:
an ancestral field is consecrated property,
and the Merciful One set it up as a redemption.
Here, it is a loan,
and it looks like interest.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the comparison made in step 1.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the comparison between a שדה אחוזה and a משכנתא
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: הקדש has no loan and its price was set by the Torah. A משכנתא is a real loan, so extra produce looks like רבית.

steps.title: רב אשי: an unspecified mortgage lasts one year
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי reports that the elders of מתא מחסיא told him that a משכנתא made without a set time lasts one year.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: The elders of מתא מחסיא told me: an unspecified משכנתא is for a year.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic. רב אשי gives a rule about a משכנתא where no time period was set.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the borrower and lender did not say how long the lender would hold the field, it is treated as lasting a year. The גמרא will next ask what practical difference this makes.

keyTerms.meaning: the town of מתא מחסיא, where רב אשי lived
a mortgage where the lender holds the field and eats its produce

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: אֲמַרוּ לִי סָבֵי דְּמָתָא מַחְסֵיָא:
phrases.english: Rav Ashi said: The elders of Mata Meḥasya told me:
An unspecified mortgage is for a year.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי אֲמַרוּ לִי סָבֵי דְּמָתָא מַחְסֵיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: New topic about a משכנתא, no longer about the dispute over the deduction.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A משכנתא made without a set time lasts at least one year.

steps.title: What difference does the one-year rule make?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what practical result comes from the rule that an unspecified משכנתא lasts a year.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the practical difference?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a short question so that it can explain the rule. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying a משכנתא lasts a year does not yet tell us what to do in practice. The גמרא wants to know when this rule actually changes the outcome.

phrases.english: What is the practical difference?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks what the rule in step 3 changes in practice.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What practical result the one-year rule has

steps.title: The borrower can remove the lender only after a year
steps.stepSummary: If the lender has eaten the produce for a year, the borrower may pay him off and remove him. Before that, he may not.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he ate from it for a year, he can remove him. If not, he cannot remove him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. The one-year rule decides when the borrower is allowed to pay back the loan and take back his field.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before a full year of produce, the lender has the right to stay on the field. After a year, the borrower can pay the debt and send the lender away. So the lender is promised at least one year of produce.

keyTerms.meaning: ate, meaning used the field's produce

phrases.aramaic: דְּאִי אָכֵיל לַהּ שַׁתָּא – מָצֵי מְסַלֵּק לֵיהּ,
phrases.english: that if he ate from it for a year, he can remove him,
phrases.notes: The one who 'ate' is the lender. 'He can remove him' means the borrower can pay up and send the lender away.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי לָא – לָא מָצֵי מְסַלֵּק לֵיהּ.
phrases.english: and if not, he cannot remove him.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאִי אָכֵיל לַהּ שַׁתָּא מָצֵי מְסַלֵּק לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 4.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The borrower cannot remove the lender before a year of produce, but he can after that.
steps.whatToRemember: A משכנתא with no set time gives the lender at least one year. Only after that can the borrower pay up and take back his field.

steps.title: רב אשי: the meaning of the word משכנתא
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי reports from the elders of מתא מחסיא that משכנתא means the field 'resides' with the lender.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב אשי said: The elders of מתא מחסיא told me: Why is it called משכנתא? Because it resides with him.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי gives a second teaching from the same elders. This one explains where the word משכנתא comes from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word משכנתא is connected to שכונה, 'residing'. The field lives with the lender, almost as if it were his own. The גמרא will next ask why this word meaning matters.

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: אֲמַרוּ לִי סָבֵי דְּמָתָא מַחְסֵיָא,
phrases.english: And Rav Ashi said: The elders of Mata Meḥasya told me:
What is 'mashkanta'? That it resides with him.
phrases.notes: A play on words: משכנתא and שכונה come from the same root, meaning 'dwelling'.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי אֲמַרוּ לִי סָבֵי דְּמָתָא מַחְסֵיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, separate teaching of רב אשי from the same elders.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A משכנתא is called that because the field resides with the lender.

steps.title: What difference does the word's meaning make?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what practical result comes from explaining משכנתא as 'residing with him'.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the practical difference?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא again asks why this matters in practice. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A word's meaning matters only if it changes a law. The גמרא wants to know which law this explanation affects.

phrases.english: What is the practical difference?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks what the explanation in step 6 changes in practice.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which law depends on the field 'residing' with the lender

steps.title: It matters for the law of the neighboring field owner
steps.stepSummary: The meaning matters for דינא דבר מצרא, the right of a neighbor to buy a bordering field first.
steps.simpleTranslation: For the law of the one whose field borders it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the word's meaning matters for the law of בר מצרא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the mortgaged field resides with the lender, he is treated somewhat like its owner. So he counts as a neighbor and gets the right of a בר מצרא to buy a bordering field before an outsider does.

keyTerms.meaning: the law giving a neighbor whose field borders the land the first right to buy it

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that a lender holding a משכנתא has a real connection to the field, close to ownership, for certain laws.

phrases.english: For the law of the one bordering [the field].
phrases.notes: Because the field 'lives' with the lender, he counts as a neighbor and gets first right to buy the field next to it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 7.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The meaning matters for the law of בר מצרא, since the lender is treated as having the field with him.
steps.whatToRemember: משכנתא means the field 'resides' with the lender. Because of this, the lender counts as a בר מצרא for the right to buy a neighboring field first.

steps.title: רבא rejects three common practices
steps.stepSummary: רבא states that the הלכה does not follow three practices: the delayed-payment pricing of רב פפא, the documents of מחוזא, and the rentals of נרש.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: The הלכה is not like the delayed-payment pricing of the people of פפונא, not like the documents of the people of מחוזא, and not like the rentals of the people of נרש.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a short list of three practices, each tied to a place or a person, and says the הלכה does not accept any of them. The גמרא will now explain each one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a new topic after the discussion of משכנתא. Each item is a business setup that some people thought was allowed but that comes close to ריבית. רבא rules against all three, and the following steps unpack them one at a time.

keyTerms.meaning: Charging a higher price for delayed payment, a hidden form of interest
Rentals of fields for a fixed amount of produce

steps.whyThisMatters: It sets the structure for the rest of the section. Each of the three practices gets its own explanation.

phrases.english: Rava said:
The halakha is not like the delayed-payment pricing of the people of Pappuna,
nor like the documents of the people of Meḥoza,
nor like the rentals of the people of Neresh.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the explanation of the word משכנתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The הלכה does not follow the טרשי of רב פפא, the documents of מחוזא, or the rentals of נרש.

steps.title: The first practice is רב פפא's delayed-payment pricing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא identifies the first item as the delayed-payment pricing of רב פפא.
steps.simpleTranslation: "The delayed-payment pricing of the people of פפונא" means the delayed-payment pricing of רב פפא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the first item on רבא's list. It points back to a known practice of רב פפא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב פפא sold goods and accepted a higher price for later payment. He thought this was allowed because he did not actually gain from it. רבא rules that the הלכה does not follow that view.

keyTerms.meaning: People of פפונא, here pointing to רב פפא

phrases.english: "Like the delayed-payment pricing of the people of Pappuna":
this means like the delayed-payment pricing of Rav Pappa.
phrases.notes: This points back to the case on 65a, where רב פפא sold liquor at a higher price for later payment.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the first item in רבא's list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The first item refers to רב פפא's practice of charging more for delayed payment.

steps.title: The documents of מחוזא and why they are a problem
steps.stepSummary: In מחוזא, people added the expected profit to the principal and wrote the total in the document. This is a problem because nobody knows there will be a profit.
steps.simpleTranslation: "The documents of מחוזא" means that they would add the profit onto the principal and write it all in the document. But who says there will be a profit?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the second practice and then gives the reason it is not allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The lender's share of a future profit was written in as if it were already earned. If the business earns less or loses money, the borrower still owes the full written amount, so he ends up paying ריבית. The question "who says there will be a profit?" is the reason for the ruling, not a real question.

keyTerms.meaning: They add or attach (a sum onto another)
The principal, the original loan amount

steps.confusionAlert: "מי יימר דהוה רווחא" is not someone challenging רבא. It explains why רבא forbids these documents.

phrases.english: "The documents of the people of Meḥoza":
that they add the profit onto the principal,
and write it in the document.
Who says there will be a profit?

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁטָרֵי מָחוֹזְנָאֵי – דְּזָקְפִי לֵיהּ לְרַוְוחָא אַקַּרְנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the second item in רבא's list and gives the reason it is forbidden.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Writing expected profit into the loan document is forbidden because the profit is not certain, so the borrower may end up paying ריבית.

steps.title: מר בר אמימר says his father did this
steps.stepSummary: מר בר אמימר tells רב אשי that his father אמימר wrote such documents, but believed borrowers who said they earned less.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר בר אמימר said to רב אשי: My father does this, and when they come before him, he believes them.
steps.whatsHappening: מר בר אמימר pushes back against the ban on the documents of מחוזא. He points out that his own father, a great חכם, used them in a careful way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His point is that the problem from the previous step can be fixed. If the lender believes the borrower who says the profit was smaller, the debt goes down to the real amount, and no ריבית is paid. This suggests the documents could be allowed with that safeguard.

keyTerms.meaning: The son of the אמורא אמימר
He believes them (trusts the borrowers' word)

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ מָר בַּר אַמֵּימָר לְרַב אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: Mar bar Ameimar said to Rav Ashi:
Father does this,
phrases.notes: He means his father writes the expected profit into the loan document.

phrases.english: and when they come before him, he believes them.
phrases.notes: When borrowers say they earned less, he trusts them and lowers the debt.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ מָר בַּר אַמֵּימָר לְרַב אָשֵׁי: אַבָּא עָבֵיד הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ban on the documents of מחוזא by citing a respected חכם who used them.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that the documents of מחוזא are forbidden.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: אמימר used these documents and avoided ריבית by trusting the borrower about the actual profit. So the documents can be used safely.

steps.title: רב אשי: what happens when the orphans hold the document?
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי answers that the safeguard works only while the lender is alive. If he dies, his orphans will collect the full amount written in the document.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: That works while he himself is here. If he dies and the document comes into the hands of the orphans, what then?
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי rejects the argument from אמימר's practice. He shows that the safeguard has a gap.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The safeguard depends on the lender personally knowing that the profit in the document was only an estimate. His יתומים would not know that. They would demand the full written sum, and the borrower would end up paying ריבית. So the documents stay forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: That works out fine (only in this case)
Orphans, the heirs of the lender

steps.whatToRemember: The documents of מחוזא are forbidden. Even a lender who trusts the borrower cannot prevent ריבית once the document passes to his heirs.

phrases.english: He said to him:
This works where he himself is present,

phrases.aramaic: אִי שָׁכֵיב וְנָפֵל שְׁטָרָא קַמֵּי יַתְמֵי, מַאי?
phrases.english: but if he dies and the document falls before the orphans, what then?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: תִּינַח הֵיכָא דְּאִיתֵיהּ לְדִידֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects מר בר אמימר's defense of his father's practice.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the idea that trusting the borrower makes the documents of מחוזא allowed.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The safeguard depends on the lender being alive. His orphans would collect the full written amount, which would be ריבית.

steps.title: An innocent remark, and אמימר dies
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא comments that רב אשי's words were like an error that goes out from a ruler, and אמימר died soon after.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was "like an error that goes out from a ruler," and אמימר died.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes the story with a short sad note. רב אשי's question about the lender dying came true, and אמימר passed away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אשי only meant to describe a possible case. But the words of a great חכם can carry weight, like a ruler's mistaken order that still gets carried out. The פסוק is used to show that his remark came true.

keyTerms.meaning: His soul rested, meaning he died

phrases.english: It was "like an error that goes out from before the ruler"
and Ameimar died.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a closing story to רב אשי's answer, showing that his example of the lender dying came true.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב אשי's innocent remark about the lender dying came true, and אמימר died.

steps.title: The leases of נרש: leasing back a field the lender never owned
steps.stepSummary: In נרש, documents said the borrower mortgaged his field to the lender and then leased it back. The גמרא asks when the lender ever owned the field, so how could he lease it out?
steps.simpleTranslation: The leases of נרש: they would write, 'So-and-so mortgaged his land to so-and-so, and then leased it back from him.' But when did the lender ever acquire the land, that he could lease it back to the borrower?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the third practice on its list, the 'leases of נרש', and shows why it is a problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A mortgaged field still belongs to the borrower. The lender holds it only as security. So the 'rent' the borrower pays is not real rent. It is extra money paid for the loan, which is ריבית.

keyTerms.meaning: The leases of נרש, a town where this contract was used
Mortgaged, gave as security for a loan
Leased it, rented the field for a fixed payment

steps.confusionAlert: Here the lender does not own the field. He only holds it as security, so he has nothing real to rent out.

phrases.english: The leases of the people of Neresh:
that they write like this:
So-and-so mortgaged his land to so-and-so,
and then he leased it back from him.
When did he acquire it,
that he could transfer it back to him?
phrases.notes: This is a rhetorical question. The lender never owned the field, so the 'rent' is really payment for the loan.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the מחוזא documents (steps 11-14) to the next item on the list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Leasing a mortgaged field back to the borrower is ריבית, since the lender never acquired the field.

steps.title: A newer wording: 'we acquired it, waited, then leased it'
steps.stepSummary: Nowadays documents are written to say the lender acquired the field, waited a while, and only then leased it back. This is said to be permitted so that people can still get loans.
steps.simpleTranslation: And nowadays, when we write, 'We acquired it from him, waited some time, and then he leased it back,' this is done so as not to lock the door in front of borrowers. It is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא presents a newer contract wording that tries to fix the problem of נרש, and says it is allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new wording says outright that the lender acquired the field first. That seems to answer the question 'when did he acquire it?' The reason given for allowing it is practical: without it, lenders would stop lending.

keyTerms.meaning: Locking the door in front of borrowers, meaning making loans unavailable

phrases.english: And nowadays, when we write like this:
"We acquired it from him
and we waited some time,
and then he leased it back,"
so as not to lock the door
in front of borrowers —
it is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a modern wording that seems to avoid the problem raised in step 15.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A document stating the lender acquired the field, waited, and then leased it back is permitted, so that loans stay available.

steps.title: The newer wording is rejected
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the idea that the newer wording makes the deal permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: But this is not correct.
steps.whatsHappening: In just three words, the גמרא rejects the permission it gave in the previous step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Writing 'we acquired it' does not change what really happened. The lender only holds the field as security. So the rent is still payment for the loan, and it remains forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: But it is nothing, this is not correct

steps.whatToRemember: Fancy contract wording does not fix ריבית. If the lender never truly owned the field, the 'rent' is still payment for the loan.

phrases.english: But this is not correct.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the permission given in step 16.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the whole claim that the modern document wording makes the lease permitted.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Saying the field was acquired does not make it so. The lender still holds it only as security, so the rent is ריבית.

steps.title: New משנה: a half-profit deal with a storekeeper
steps.stepSummary: The משנה forbids giving a storekeeper goods, or money to buy goods, for half the profits. It is allowed only if the storekeeper is paid a worker's wage.
steps.simpleTranslation: One may not set up a storekeeper for half the profits. Nor may one give money to buy produce for half the profits. This is allowed only if he pays the storekeeper his wage like a worker.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins, about business partnerships where the profits are split in half.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In such a deal, half the goods count as a loan to the storekeeper, since he carries the risk on that half. The other half stays the owner's. The storekeeper also works to sell the owner's half. If he does that for free, his free work is a reward for the loan, which is ריבית. Paying him a wage removes the problem.

keyTerms.meaning: משנה, the start of a new משנה

steps.confusionAlert: The profit split itself is not the problem. The problem is that the storekeeper does unpaid work on the owner's half.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the basis of the היתר עיסקא idea: an investment partnership is allowed only when the worker is paid for his work.

phrases.english: MISHNA: One may not set up a storekeeper
for half the profit,
and one may not give money
to buy produce with it
for half the profit,
unless
he gives him his wage like a worker.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה on a new form of possible ריבית.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A half-profit deal with a storekeeper, whether with goods or with money, is forbidden unless he is paid a worker's wage.

steps.title: The same rule for chickens, calves and foals
steps.stepSummary: The משנה applies the same rule to hatching chickens and raising calves or foals for half the profit. It is allowed only if the caretaker is paid for his work and for the food.
steps.simpleTranslation: One may not set chickens on eggs for half the profit. One may not value calves and foals for half the profit. This is allowed only if the owner pays him for his work and for the food.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues with a second set of cases, this time about raising animals for a split profit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here too, the caretaker does unpaid work on the owner's share, which would be a reward for a loan. Since raising animals also costs food, the owner must pay for both the labor and the feed.

keyTerms.meaning: Chickens, here set on eggs to hatch them
His food, the cost of feeding the animals

steps.whatToRemember: In every half-profit deal, the worker must be paid for his work, and for the food when he raises animals. Otherwise his free work counts as ריבית.

phrases.english: One may not set chickens on eggs for half,
phrases.notes: The owner gives eggs to someone whose hens will sit on them, and they split the chicks.

phrases.english: and one may not value calves and foals for half,
phrases.notes: The young animals are given a price, and the raiser shares the increase in their value.

phrases.english: unless he gives him
payment for his work and his food.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the storekeeper rule to raising animals.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Half-profit deals for hatching chickens or raising calves and foals are forbidden unless the caretaker is paid for his labor and food.

steps.title: Exception: raising calves, foals and donkeys for half the profit
steps.stepSummary: The משנה allows taking calves and foals to raise for half the profit until they reach a third of their growth, and a donkey until it can carry a load.
steps.simpleTranslation: But a person may take calves and foals to raise for half the profit, and raise them until they reach a third of their growth. A donkey may be raised until it is big enough to carry a load.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה finishes with a permitted way to raise calves and foals for half the earnings. It also says how long they may be raised under such a deal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 19 spoke of animals that are appraised (שָׁמִין), which makes the raiser responsible for their value, so half of them is like a loan. Here the raiser simply takes them (מְקַבְּלִין) without an appraisal, and the owner carries the loss, so there is no loan and no ריבית. The 'third of their growth' and 'until a donkey can carry a load' only say how long they are raised before the profit is split.

keyTerms.meaning: May take on (animals to raise for someone else)
Grown to a third (of their full growth)

steps.confusionAlert: Step 19 forbade raising calves and foals for half, and now the משנה allows it. This is not a contradiction. Step 19 spoke of appraised animals (שמין), while here they are simply taken on (מקבלין). The growth stage only sets how long they are raised.

phrases.english: But one may take calves and foals to raise for half,
and raise them until they reach a third.
phrases.notes: Literally 'made into thirds.' Here it means grown to a third of their full growth.

phrases.english: And a donkey, until it can carry a load.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: It contrasts with step 19: appraised animals are forbidden, but taking animals on for half without appraisal is allowed, up to a set stage of growth.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Calves and foals may be raised for half the profit until they reach a third of their growth. A donkey may be raised this way until it can carry a load.

steps.title: A ברייתא: the wage is that of an idle worker
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens by quoting a ברייתא saying the wage the משנה requires is that of a פועל בטל.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: It was taught in a ברייתא: the caretaker is paid like an idle worker.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins. It quotes a ברייתא that explains the 'worker's wage' the משנה required in steps 18 and 19.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said the storekeeper or caretaker must be paid like a worker so the deal is permitted. The ברייתא adds a detail: he is paid like a פועל בטל, an 'idle worker.' It does not yet say what that means, which leads straight into the next question.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that explains the משנה
It was taught (a ברייתא is being quoted)
An idle worker, someone not working at the moment

phrases.english: GEMARA:
It was taught: like an idle worker.
phrases.notes: This explains the 'worker's wage' the משנה required for the storekeeper or caretaker.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: It moves from the משנה to the גמרא and explains the wage the משנה required.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The wage the משנה requires is the wage of a פועל בטל.

steps.title: What does 'like an idle worker' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what it means to pay someone like a פועל בטל.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'like an idle worker' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the meaning of the phrase from the ברייתא. This sets up the explanation that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: It is not clear how much an 'idle worker' gets paid, since he is not doing his usual job. The גמרא wants to know exactly what wage counts. This is a real question, not a challenge.

phrases.english: What does 'like an idle worker' mean?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: It asks for the meaning of the term just quoted from the ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of paying the caretaker 'like a פועל בטל,' meaning what wage he is owed.
